parsed.explanation: The write-up's only route to finiteness is the purely set-theoretic lemma that a pairwise intersecting family has finitely many minimal transversals. The induction proves the criterion only for transversals X meeting C, and at every level below the first C\{c} need not lie in F_c, so the quoted justification is unavailable; the objection's F={{1,2},{2,3}}, C={2}, X={1,3} shows a transversal disjoint from C, so the derived list misses transversals and the recursion fails. Worse, the lemma is outright false (ledger L6.2: F_k={x_1..x_k,y_k} is pairwise intersecting with infinitely many minimal transversals). No arithmetic large-prime erasure argument appears anywhere in the text, so finiteness is unproved and the approach itself is wrong.
